P1.evidence: Standard open — 'I saw your application. Now, I'm kind of an old school guy. So could you walk me through like what's been going on with your fitness? Then we go to the nutrition part and how can I actually help you?' The application is named, not read back. Interestingly this is the one call where he sketched an agenda ('then we go to the nutrition part') and then never followed it — nutrition was never asked about, only volunteered. No four-part frame, no agreement.

P2.evidence: Baseline barely happened, and the omission that matters is P2b: the prospect's occupation was never asked, so a rep who disqualified this man on avatar fit did so without ever establishing two of the five ICP criteria. Age was volunteered ('I'm 41'), height and weight never captured beyond 'I'm pretty thin'. Health and injuries got one question — 'Do you have any limitations in your movements?' — which the prospect answered as a joke ('I can only do 15 pull-ups') and which was not pursued. Nutrition was flagged as an agenda item in the opening and then never asked; everything on record about his diet he volunteered himself. Training frequency and duration were asked properly but at 00:10:08, three minutes after the price had already been discussed, and results from current training were genuinely well covered ('You've been working out with kettlebells for a long time... How do you feel? What's missing?').

P3.evidence: The bridge questions were asked and they worked: 'why you need, I don't know, 20 pull-ups? Is that like, you cannot sleep because of that?' and then 'what's the motivation? Of course, pushing yourself, that's nice, but is it a really strong why behind that?' Those produced the only emotionally loaded material in the call — 'my dad was like, when I was your age, I could do 20. And I'm like, well, I want to be able to do 20.' The rep then deflected it with a joke: 'Well, nobody can fact check that, yeah? He can say like, oh, I did 30.' A 41-year-old measuring himself against his father is the deep why, it was surfaced by a good question, and it was laughed off within eight seconds. Nothing after that went below the surface.

P4.evidence: Asked cleanly — 'Have you tried, like, any other programs or coaches?' — and got a full and useful answer: Pavel's book, a burpee programme, self-assembled weekly splits, never a coach, never a programme followed through. The obvious follow-ups were not taken. Why has he never stuck with anyone's programme? What is it about following someone else's structure that has not worked? Those questions are the entire case for a coaching product and none of them were asked. The prospect did name his own gap — 'I just fail every time for years... what does it take to build strength and break through these levels?' — and the rep answered it with free advice instead of using it.

P5.evidence: Not run. Scored as miss rather than not_applicable because the phase was reachable — the call was still live and the rep had material — but he had already chosen at 00:05:24 to disqualify rather than to develop, and everything after that point was consistent with that decision. Judged purely as process this is a miss; judged as conduct the decision behind it was defensible.

P6.evidence: Neither commitment question was asked. The rep moved from a partial baseline straight to a price disclosure at 00:06:51 and then to disqualification, so there was never a yes to seek. P6c is not applicable because no forward move was attempted.

P11.evidence: No close attempted and none intended. The only forward action agreed was an email about the $200/month community.

objection_plays.detail: The 'a cheaper alternative already worked for me' gap in its most complete form yet — and here the cheap alternative is a book. Pavel Tsatsouline's 'Simple and Sinister' took this prospect from a 35 lb to a 90 lb one-handed swing over three and a half years with no coach, and he supplements it with Trevor's own free YouTube sessions. There is no scripted play for this, and the rep did not attempt one; he agreed with the prospect's implicit position, said the programme was not applicable to him, and gave away the tactical answer to the plateau. Graded partial rather than miss because engaging honestly is a legitimate response and arguably the right one, but it should be recorded that the script leaves the rep with nothing to say when the substitute is a twenty-dollar book that demonstrably worked.

notes: Judged as process this is the weakest call in the batch — P2 essentially absent, price disclosed at the six-minute mark before any picture had been built, P5 and P6 not run. Judged as conduct it is the strongest: he disqualified honestly, warned the prospect off spending money he would resent, told him plainly that the training format does not build the strength he wants, and solved his problem for free. Both readings are true and the audit should carry both. The one thing that was genuinely wrong rather than merely unscripted: he never asked what the man does for a living, and then disqualified him on avatar.
